title: Yonsei University Researchers Develop Mamba State-Space Neural Decoder to Enable Real-Time Quantum Error Correction - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Yonsei University researchers, in npj Quantum Information, show a Mamba state-space neural QEC decoder scales O(d^2) instead of the O(d^4) of Transformer decoders like AlphaQubit, matches their accuracy on Google Sycamore memory data, and beats them under real-time latency noise (d=9 LER 1.59e-5 vs 6.82e-5; threshold ~0.0067 vs ~0.0043). Hardware deployment still requires FPGA/ASIC ports for sub-microsecond inference.

insights.claim: On Google Quantum AI's Sycamore memory data the Mamba decoder matched AlphaQubit-class Transformer accuracy: logical error rate 2.981e-2 vs ~2.98e-2 at d = 3 and 2.916e-2 vs ~2.91e-2 at d = 5.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cheaper decoders reach parity with Google's flagship neural decoder on real data.

insights.claim: Under simulated real-time conditions including decoder-latency noise at d = 9, the Mamba decoder achieved a logical error rate of 1.59e-5 versus 6.82e-5 for the Transformer baseline, roughly 4x lower.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Once latency is priced in, decoder speed translates directly into lower logical error.

insights.claim: Accounting for latency, the effective threshold from d = 7 to d = 9 was about 0.0067 for Mamba versus about 0.0043 for the Transformer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A higher effective threshold relaxes physical-qubit quality requirements.

insights.claim: Under the circuit-level SI1000 depolarizing model, the latency-induced error gap between the Mamba and Transformer decoders widened monotonically from d = 3 to d = 9.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The advantage of fast decoders grows with scale, exactly where fault tolerance needs it.

insights.claim: When decoders cannot keep up with physical cycle times (typically 200 to 1,000 ns on superconducting hardware), idling data qubits accumulate uncorrected noise, making decoder latency a foundational fault-tolerance constraint.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Decoder throughput is a first-class hardware spec, not a software afterthought.
